title: Token Habitat: Cost Composer & Attribution Canvas
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create a compact, role-aware UI pattern for token-level cost breakdowns that supports interactive attribution, CSV/NDJSON export, and quick drilldowns. The goal is a single composer canvas (Token Habitat) where users can: pivot cost by model/route/user/organization, splice cost into origin buckets (prefix cache hits, KV cache, batching delta, rerank), tag chargebacks, and export filtered line items for downstream finance or SRE processes. This design must balance density (high information per screen) with clarity for non-engineering finance users.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas supports pivoting by Model, Route, User, and Time window with persisted selections
CSV and NDJSON export include metadata columns (request_id, model_variant, route_id, user_segment, kv_cache_hit, prefix_length, token_count, unit_cost)
Role-aware export options: Finance export (aggregate by SKU), SRE export (request trace IDs + latency buckets), Product export (prompts + model variant)
UI shows clear attribution waterfall (base token cost -> batching delta -> cache savings -> fallback surcharge) with percentage and absolute columns
Prototype validated in 2 usability sessions with at least 80% task completion for 'create export for billing' task
Design tokens and spacing conform to console theme; components documented in the pattern library with responsive behaviors

tradeoffs: Density vs discoverability: Chosen compact default improves power-user efficiency but may hide explanations for casual viewers; mitigated via toggles and tooltips
Client-side vs server-side export generation: Server-side required for very large exports; prototype supports client preview only until backend fields are ready
Row-level detail vs aggregated view: We expose both but default to aggregated SKU-first view to reduce noise for finance users
